summary: Freight invoices need reconciliation against rate contracts because carrier billing frequently contains errors such as incorrect base rates, duplicate charges, and unauthorized accessorial or surcharge fees that only surface through line-by-line comparison with the negotiated contract terms. Without systematic matching of invoiced amounts to contracted rates, small discrepancies compound across thousands of shipments into significant, hard-to-recover overpayments. Beyond direct cost recovery, consistent reconciliation improves freight spend visibility and data quality, strengthening carrier performance scorecards, budgeting accuracy, and negotiating leverage in future rate discussions. It also supports compliance and dispute resolution by giving shippers documented evidence when contesting incorrect charges or renegotiating carrier terms.
